title: Trump Heads to Shenzhen Summit as Xi Urges Open Trade, NSA Classified Network Goes Down Amid US Outages, and Haitians Rally Behind Salvadoran Troops
subhead: US President Donald Trump prepares to fly from the Philippines to Shenzhen for a trilateral summit with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin as Xi urges removing trade barriers; a classified communications network at the US National Security Agency goes dark even as Secretary of State Marco Rubio sees no cyberattack link across recent US outages; and thousands in Haiti rally in support of Salvadoran anti-gang forces.

sections.heading: Trump Heads Toward Shenzhen Trilateral Summit as Xi Urges Removing Trade Barriers
sections.body:
New York Times, CNBC, and Financial Times — US President Donald Trump is meeting Philippine leadership in Manila before flying to Shenzhen, China, for a trilateral summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin (New York Times). Ahead of the gathering, Xi called for removing global trade and investment barriers while Beijing showcased Shenzhen as a high-tech showcase city after cleaning up illicit markets for APEC attendees (CNBC, Financial Times). Yet domestic economic momentum in China continues to slow even as foreign demand for Chinese exports surges, creating mixed economic conditions for Beijing going into trade talks (Wall Street Journal).

Russian President Vladimir Putin is also scheduled to address global CEOs in China before sitting down with Xi and Trump (Financial Times). Meanwhile, New York Times noted that Xi's summit showcase faces headwinds from export friction, a high-profile espionage scandal, and Trump's unpredictability, with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio reiterating that Trump remains willing to meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un (Anadolu Agency).
sections.whyItMatters: The Shenzhen summit brings Trump, Xi, and Putin into direct face-to-face talks over trade, security, and great-power competition at a moment when both Washington and Beijing face domestic economic and political pressures.

sections.heading: Kuwait and Bahrain Counter Drone and Missile Attacks as Iran Threatens Symmetrical Nuclear Response
sections.body:
France 24 and Anadolu Agency — Kuwait's military announced Wednesday it was countering hostile drone attacks while Bahrain reported intercepting Iranian aerial strikes, keeping US-allied Gulf states on high alert after a US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island (France 24). In Tehran, a member of parliament's national security committee warned that Iran would respond 'at the same level' if struck by a US nuclear weapon and expressed deep skepticism about reaching any agreement with Washington (Anadolu Agency).

In Yemen, the Saudi-led coalition reported destroying 60 Houthi targets in operations aimed at degrading ballistic missile and drone capabilities, while Yemen's government army said it neutralized 178 Houthi fighters across 660 strikes on Houthi positions (Anadolu Agency). Despite the active Gulf fighting, CNA reported benchmark oil prices eased early Wednesday as higher US crude inventories tempered near-term supply concerns.
sections.whyItMatters: Direct drone and missile interceptions over Kuwait and Bahrain show the US-Iran confrontation actively spilling across Gulf Cooperation Council airspace even as crude markets absorb supply shocks.

sections.heading: NSA Classified Network Goes Down Amid US Disruptions as CISA Warns on Oracle Java Flaw
sections.body:
AP News, Anadolu Agency, and Financial Times — A classified communications network at the US National Security Agency went down, a defense official confirmed to AP News, adding to a week of rolling US infrastructure disruptions that have locked customers out of bank accounts, grounded flights, and halted emails (Axios). US Secretary of State Marco Rubio insisted there is 'zero' or 'no evidence' linking the Microsoft, FAA, and banking outages to each other or to a malign cyberactor (AP News, Anadolu Agency).

At the same time, the US cybersecurity agency warned banks, corporations, and government agencies to patch systems running Oracle's Java programming language over a critical vulnerability (Financial Times). On Wall Street, Nvidia beat sales expectations and rejected ousted founder Jensen Huang's offer to return as CEO even as the SEC opened an investigation into the chipmaker (AP News, Bloomberg, TechCrunch).
sections.whyItMatters: Consecutive outages across aviation, banking, and now an NSA classified network underscore growing fragility in core US digital systems even without evidence of coordinated sabotage.

sections.heading: Russian Military Plane Crash Kills 19 as EU Fast-Tracks Grid Permits and France Sees Mass Marches
sections.body:
The Independent, Anadolu Agency, and Le Monde — A Russian military aircraft crashed in Siberia, killing all 19 people on board on a day of mounting military setbacks for Moscow (The Independent). In Brussels, European Union negotiators reached a provisional agreement to fast-track permits for renewable energy projects and electricity grids to accelerate critical infrastructure deployment and reinforce European energy security (Anadolu Agency).

Across Western Europe, domestic political pressures sharpened: Le Monde reported that Germany—which absorbed nearly one million Syrians since 2015—has joined four other EU states in considering migrant 'return centers' in Rwanda for rejected asylum seekers. In France, Tuesday's November 17 protests from Paris to Lyon drew 146,000 demonstrators according to the Interior Ministry and over 500,000 according to the CGT union, sending a warning ahead of the next Elysée race (Le Monde).
sections.whyItMatters: Europe is simultaneously accelerating energy-grid permitting to cut external energy vulnerability while shifting rightward on migration enforcement amid widespread domestic labor and cost-of-living protests.

sections.heading: Haitians Rally Behind Salvadoran Troops as Sudan's Army Advances in West Kordofan
sections.body:
France 24, AP News, and Anadolu Agency — Thousands of Haitians marched in Port-au-Prince on Tuesday urging El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele to keep fighting armed gangs, praising Salvadoran troops currently deployed alongside local security forces in the Caribbean nation (France 24, AP News). The public rally reflects intense popular demand for security restoration in gang-dominated neighborhoods.

In Africa, the Sudanese army gained ground in West Kordofan as the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces retreated, though humanitarian groups appealed for urgent food and medical deliveries in Al-Khuway (Anadolu Agency). Meanwhile, in South America, SCMP reported that roughly 20 Indigenous people emerged thin and hungry from isolation in Brazil's Amazon rainforest, raising alarm over growing illegal incursions into protected territory.
sections.whyItMatters: Public backing in Haiti for El Salvador's security deployment highlights how regional states are stepping into policing vacuums where traditional multilateral interventions have struggled.

bottomLine: Wednesday's global picture centers on high-stakes summit diplomacy and widening operational strain: Donald Trump is heading toward Shenzhen for trilateral talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin as Beijing urges open trade, Kuwait and Bahrain are intercepting aerial attacks across the Gulf, an NSA classified network went down amid rolling US infrastructure outages, and Europe moved to fast-track grid permits while debating offshore asylum hubs in Rwanda.
